decisive_items: After 10 days of fever with an absolute neutrophil count of 20/μL, she reported severe pain in her right arm radiating to her shoulder
High-resolution chest CT showed nonspecific nodules under 1 cm
MRI of the right shoulder demonstrated a focal cystic necrotic lesion between the teres minor and teres major muscles
response.rationale: In a persistently neutropenic patient with antibiotic-refractory fever, pulmonary nodules, and a focal necrotic muscular lesion, invasive fungal infection is the most likely unifying diagnosis. The negative galactomannan does not exclude all invasive fungi, and the clinical-radiographic pattern favors an opportunistic mold infection over the broader or earlier entities.

rejected.why: Febrile neutropenia explains the fever risk but not the focal MRI lesion, pulmonary nodules, or persistent failure to improve.
Herpes zoster was considered clinically, but no vesicles were present and the MRI showed a necrotic soft-tissue lesion rather than a dermatomal vesicular rash.
ALL is the already established underlying leukemia, not the new cause of the painful shoulder mass.
Coagulase-negative staphylococcal bacteremia was treated and would not explain a focal necrotic muscular lesion developing on broad-spectrum antibiotics.
Soft tissue infection is nondescriptive and less specific; the lesion is best contextualized in this immunocompromised host as an invasive fungal infection.
